supersedes: The same-layer interval inference and per-particle full-profile validation of rejected v1 are not in this reviewed source.

checks.detail: Initial Height=0 cannot produce a false hit because Index starts at 0 and reuse requires Index>0. The first query always calls the unchanged BinarySearch.
Only the same finite numeric Height reuses the previous positive Index. Changed height, NaN and either infinity call the original function. No same-layer or adjacent-layer inference remains.

Float == treats +0 and -0 as equal. The unchanged search uses ordered comparisons only, so both return the same layer for an immutable profile; the actual wind interpolation still uses the current f1 and preserves its sign.

There is no profile scan or lower-bound inference. Memoisation repeats the original function value for an unchanged height and unchanged immutable input profile, so duplicate/nonmonotone/nonfinite profile behaviour is retained.
HOKART reference or NKK change replaces the state and resets Index to 0 before any cache reuse. A default state (Levels null) goes directly to the original function.

Current HOKART values and NKK are initialised before dispersion. No assignment during particle tracking was found. Arbitrary in-place mutation while the same state is live is outside the contract; a new particle uses a fresh state.

The original 6-argument IntWindCalculate method and tuple remain. It delegates with default state, leaving its binary search unchanged. The overload changes the lookup call only; terrain interpolation equations, casts and evaluation order remain, as do flat/building and deposition-call paths.

Both drivers initialise local state only for terrain and reuse it in selected terrain interpolation/reflection searches. No cross-particle state, RNG edits, scheduling changes or lock changes are in the topic diff.
The earlier one-line stack topic remains separate. Its write-before-read proof remains valid. Full NS=512/513 tracking is not established by the four declaration-entry component assertions alone.

recorded_profile.scope: Two synthetic terrain projects: hot N=100 and stable/building N=1000, each repeated twice. Test-only Interlocked counters inspect routing and alter timing. This is not a speed benchmark or a production hit-rate distribution.

publication_eligibility: Suitable only for a focused Draft evaluation of exact-height reuse with explicit changed-height overhead and measured synthetic routing. Source correctness is supported; a general whole-model optimization claim is not supported.
limits: Reviewer performed source/diff/fixture/data review only; did not rerun DLL tests, Main, timing or instrumentation.
Standalone lookup measurements include fresh state preparation and only the lookup workload. Whole-model speedup is not established.
Same-height 15 measured cases are faster; 29 changed-height cases take 4.3259% to 28.1352% longer; one changed-height case is slightly faster. All 45 conditions must remain visible.
The actual ~50% hit fraction supports cache use in two selected synthetic projects but does not establish a production workload distribution or a full-model speedup.
Fixed-seed one-worker invariance does not imply identical clock-seeded or multiworker shared-sum results.
No automatic detection of arbitrary in-place HOKART edits within a live particle is claimed.
Shared baseline executions are counted as executed; validation is not a per-patch independent factorial design.
Superseded, preliminary and harness-debug runs are preserved but excluded from final counts.
Main elapsed times are watchdog evidence, not optimization benchmarks.
Terrain path is exercised, but terrain reflection occurrence counts are not instrumented in these ordinary source runs.
All terrain and prescribed wind input are entirely synthetic; no GRAMM solver run or production-domain scientific truth is asserted.
